newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador to privatisate some state firms.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador to privatisate some state firms.

text.p: Ecuador's new government will sell off part or all of some state firms including telecoms, utilities, railways and the customs service, but is not keen on mass privatisations, an administration official said on Monday.

"There are certain sectors of the economy that may be better managed by the private enterprise, leaving the obsolete state to handle those areas where it can better serve the community," National Council on Modernisation President Rodrigo Paz told foreign correspondents.
"Nevertheless, I don't agree with the selling of the state's assets," he said. "... We should not think that privatisations will solve all problems."
Plans to privatise public companies under the government of former President Abadala Bucaram had been called into doubt after the fall of his administration.

After he was declared mentally incompetent and removed from office by Congress in February, both the new government and Congress said the sale of telephone company Emetel would be subject to review and probably postponed.
But Paz said on Monday that the sale of 35 percent of Emetel would go ahead as planned and that bids would be revealed in late April.
U.S. firms MCI and GTE Corp, Italy's Stet, Spain's Telefonica and Korea Telecom all signed up for the Emetel partial privatisation last November.

Paz said the customs service would also be sold but that the state would seek a non-profit organization as its buyer. Control of the country's railways will also be handed over to private companies, he said.
The official said several different options were under study to raise capital for the electricity utility.
"There is great international interest... We have given ourselves one month to clarify this situation," Paz said.
